name: Binaural Experiments
description: Headphone studies that treat the two ears as two instruments: beats that form between the ears, delays that move and widen a sound, phase and noise that spread it around your head, a tune hidden in noise, split spectra, wandering filters and a classic dichotic illusion. Each sketch explains what to listen for and what changes on speakers or in mono. Headphones on, volume low.
author: Claude, for Tartlet

sketches.name: Beat or Pulse
sketches.description: Two bars of a 5 Hz binaural beat, then two bars of plain amplitude pulsing at the same rate. The first only exists on headphones; the second is audible on speakers too. The player asks before playing, as with any steady pulse.

sketches.name: Cents Apart
sketches.description: A drone whose ears drift apart in cents, two bars at a time: 2 cents beats slowly, 6 and 12 shimmer, and 30 widens into a chorus. A plain centred sine stays put as a reference.

sketches.name: Haas Corridor
sketches.description: Interaural time differences. A pluck swings from side to side on delays under a millisecond, while a pad stays on the leading side and grows wider as its delay rises to 8 and 20 ms.

sketches.name: Inside the Head
sketches.description: Interaural phase. In phase, the drone sits in the centre of your head; at 90 degrees it loosens; at 180 it spreads diffusely around you. On speakers or in mono, the 180-degree bar nearly vanishes.

sketches.name: Correlation Ladder
sketches.description: Pink noise steps down from identical in both ears to almost independent in each. A point in the middle of your head opens into a wide, enveloping wash.

sketches.name: Hidden Melody
sketches.description: Each ear alone hears only white noise. Together, a faint tune appears between them (Huggins pitch). A quiet sine plays the first phrase every four bars, so you know what to listen for. The effect is faint and differs between listeners.

sketches.name: Split Spectrum
sketches.description: Spectral fusion. A pad sends alternate partials to each ear and the drums split lows from highs at 900 Hz. Neither ear hears the whole sound; together, and in mono, it sounds complete.

sketches.name: Wandering Brightness
sketches.description: Nothing is panned, yet the brightness drifts from ear to ear: an arpeggio has a low-pass on each ear alone, sweeping in opposite directions. The pad underneath is thinner in one ear than the other.

sketches.name: Ear Hops
sketches.description: Bells lean to the right with a level difference between the ears, and a patterned ear swap flips some of them to the left, so the melody hops between your ears.
sketches.source:
setcpm(90/4)

// ild makes the right ear louder; earswap flips the ears on the steps marked 1
bells: n("0 4 2 5 4 7 5 9").scale("C:major").transpose(12).s("sine").fm(2).fmh(3)
  .ild(9).earswap("0 1 0 1 1 0 1 0")
  .decay(.3).sustain(0).release(.4).gain(.22)

// A softer counter-line that swaps once per bar
counter: n("<[0 ~ 2 ~] [4 ~ 2 ~]>").scale("C:major").s("triangle").timbre("soft")
  .ild(6).earswap("<0 1>").decay(.4).sustain(.2).release(.4).gain(.16)

// A centred kit and bass
drums: s("bd ~ ~ bd, ~ rim ~ rim").gain(.35)
bass: note("<c2 a1 f1 g1>").s("sine").attack(.02).sustain(.6).release(.3).gain(.32)

sketches.name: Scale Illusion
sketches.description: Diana Deutsch's scale illusion. A rising and a falling C major scale are played together, alternating ears on every note. Each ear's part jumps around, but many listeners hear smooth lines regroup by pitch instead.
sketches.source:
setcpm(60/4)

// A rising and a falling scale, alternating ears on every note
// Each ear's part jumps around; many listeners hear smooth lines grouped by pitch instead
right: note("c5 d4 a4 f4 f4 a4 d4 c5").s("sine").pan(1)
  .attack(.01).decay(.3).sustain(.5).release(.1).gain(.3)
left: note("c4 b4 e4 g4 g4 e4 b4 c4").s("sine").pan(0)
  .attack(.01).decay(.3).sustain(.5).release(.1).gain(.3)

sketches.name: Slow Rotation
sketches.description: The phase between the ears turns continuously, once every four seconds, then every two, then once and twice a second. The drone seems to roll around inside your head, staying below the rates that trigger a pulse warning.
